note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Build those first 3 starting with ledger first"; of the 21 countries read first: "It should cover across every country"; "Retry the blocked tax facts once all countries land"): the tax on a screen worker's pay in Thailand: a resident's income tax, social contributions, what is withheld at source, a non-resident artiste's withholding, an author's treatment, VAT and the tax year. Research and retry subagents (workbench/briefs/BRIEF-tax.md, BRIEF-tax-retry.md), every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: Net income is taxed at 0% to THB 150,000, then 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25% and 30% up to THB 5 million, and 35% above; there is no regional layer.
Before the scale, employment income gets a 50% standard deduction capped at THB 100,000, and each taxpayer a personal allowance of THB 60,000; social security contributions are deductible.

sources.said: A standard deduction of 50%, with a limit of THB 100,000, is permitted in respect of income from employment.
Personal allowances There is a personal allowance of THB 60,000 each for the taxpayer

figures.finding: The tax year is the calendar year; the return is due by 31 March (8 April online); business and some other income also needs a half-year return by 30 September.

sources.said: The tax year is the calendar year.
All persons earning income are required to file a tax return no later than 31 March of the following year for hardcopy filing and 8 April for online filing
Individuals engaged in most forms of business are also required to file a return of their income for the first six months of the year by 30 September and pay the tax due.

figures.finding: The payer withholds from employment income at the progressive rates, 3% from service and professional fees, and 5% from a Thai-resident public entertainer's pay; tax withheld is credited on the annual return.

sources.said: The tax withheld shall then be credited against tax liability of a taxpayer at the time of filing PIT return.
4. Service and professional fees 3 % 5. Public entertainer remuneration - Thai resident - non resident 5 % 5 - 37 %

figures.finding: A non-resident is taxed on Thai-source income. A public entertainer (actor in theatre, film, radio or TV, singer, musician) domiciled abroad has tax withheld at the personal income tax schedule's progressive rates, except a foreign-domiciled film or TV actor in a foreign company's production permitted to shoot in Thailand, withheld at 10%; tax withheld is credited on the annual return, so it is not final. A non-resident's other fees for work (Section 40(2)) are withheld at 15%.
figures.applies: 2026 (Order Tor.Por.4/2528 clause 9(2) as amended by Tor.Por.111/2545; Revenue Code s. 50(1)). The RD's English table still prints the pre-2017 scale '5 - 37 %'; the schedule now in force is in the residents figure.

sources.said: A non-resident is, however, subject to tax only on income from sources in Thailand.
Public entertainer remuneration - Thai resident - non resident 5 % 5 - 37 %

In the case of paying assessable income under Section 40 (2), other than as described in paragraph 3, to a non-resident, withholding tax shall be made at the rate of 15.0 per cent of the income.
The tax withheld shall then be credited against tax liability of a taxpayer at the time of filing PIT return.

figures.finding: Employee, employer and government each pay 5% of salary to the social security fund, the employee's share capped at THB 875 a month.

sources.said: All employees are required to contribute to a social security fund an amount equal to 5% of their salary, up to a maximum contribution of THB 875 per month. Employers and the government are also required to contribute an equal amount.

figures.finding: VAT is 10% by law but reduced to 7% until 30 September 2027; a business whose tax base (turnover) does not exceed THB 1.8 million a year, counted by calendar year for an individual, is exempt from VAT but may register.
figures.applies: 2026 (Royal Decree No. 432 B.E. 2548 in force from 1 April 2005 under Revenue Code s. 81/1).

sources.said: The standard rate of VAT is 10%, but the rate is currently reduced to 7% until 30 September 2027 (unless further extended by the government).
